assumptions.assumption: The generate_html f-string's server-side interpolations are data-shaped (values, flags, lists) rather than structural (Python conditionals/loops emitting HTML blocks), so the frontend can move verbatim with only a small window.ANCHOR_BOOT bootstrap JSON; if a material fraction of the ~2,700-line f-string is server-composed markup from the ~2,800 lines of _render_* helpers, the extraction stops being a parity-preserving move and the >=7,000-line shrink target becomes unreachable without restructuring the North Star forbids (no UI redesign).
assumptions.basis: Stage-0 T2 itself flags the bootstrap-JSON replacement as 'the only genuinely fiddly part of Pillar 1' but never counts the interpolation sites or classifies them data-vs-structure; C1's line-count bar (~8,600 embedded lines minus ~50-line allowance) only closes if essentially all three blobs extract clean.

assumptions.assumption: Playwright verification of the home dashboard and the project window is a sufficient proxy for behavior parity across ~4,660 lines of client JS whose surface includes WS terminals, SSE fallback, pending-paste flush, drag-to-group, window maximize/resize, and the v12 dock — flows a page-load smoke test never exercises.
assumptions.basis: C1 names exactly two Playwright targets; the CLAUDE.md history shows every prior UI wave needed screenshot + interactive sign-off precisely because render-level checks missed interaction regressions (the v4 lesson).

assumptions.assumption: ANCHOR_TOKEN is (or will be) actually set on the live NSSM deployment, making default-deny real rather than vacuous — C2 gates the GET data plane only 'when ANCHOR_TOKEN is set', so if the live service runs tokenless the entire auth pillar ships as dead code on the box it was built to protect.
assumptions.basis: The anchor-as-app research memory records ANCHOR_TOKEN as a known gap ('mandatory before Tailscale exposure'), implying the live service today runs without it; nothing in the North Star mandates turning it on or defines the ops step (elevated nssm env edit + restart) to do so.

assumptions.assumption: Cookie-based auth can be layered onto every existing browser consumer without breakage: the hand-rolled RFC-6455 upgrade path can read the Cookie header, EventSource/SSE and every _postJson fetch keep working, the first-visit token-to-cookie handshake is usable from non-desktop clients (iPhone PWA over Tailscale), and the CLI mirror / healthcheck / any localhost scripts that today hit the open GET plane get a token path — otherwise the strangler migration hits a flag-day where all consumers must flip at once, violating C7.
assumptions.basis: GAP-2 is acknowledged as a design decision but the consumer census (WS upgrade, SSE, healthcheck's endpoint walk, anchor.py mirrors, PWA/Tailscale usage from the anchor-as-app plan) is nowhere enumerated; D3 locks cookie mechanics before that census exists.

assumptions.assumption: The set of mutation-of-record write sites is closed and bounded to the four named modules (effort_history, session_registry, terminal_session, job_runner) — i.e., no handler in anchor_gui.py or elsewhere mutates index/pointer/registry/grass/boneyard state directly — so journal instrumentation can be complete and the parity gate's 'zero divergence' is achievable rather than a permanent red.
assumptions.basis: GAP-3 asserts 'the write sites are all in effort_history/session_registry/terminal_session/job_runner' as an unverified claim; anchor_gui.py's change-ops section (10531–10964) and 4,300-line handler class historically contain direct writes (log_change, project record edits, rnd_registry mutations), and one missed site makes C3's gate fail by construction.

assumptions.assumption: 'Zero divergence' between journal-derived and legacy-derived views is a stable, testable property despite (a) dual-write being non-atomic across journal append and legacy store write (a crash or exception between the two manufactures divergence), (b) the legacy stores' own known lossiness (the very torn-write class the journal exists to fix), and (c) the daily healthcheck deriving views while the live service concurrently writes — a flaky parity gate re-lights the red banner John was just trained to trust.
assumptions.basis: C3 demands the gate in tests AND the daily healthcheck with zero divergence, but Stage-0's own Pillar-3 analysis proves per-file atomicity without cross-file transactionality; the same crash-window argument applies verbatim to the new journal+legacy write pair, and no divergence-tolerance or ordering contract is specified.

assumptions.assumption: Jobs and PTYs are cleanly separable ownership domains: every 'lane job' interaction the dashboard offers — tail cursors, cancel/tree-kill, AskUserQuestion gate answers written onto held stdin, token/cost accounting, swarm-session registration — can be proxied over loopback IPC to a supervisor-held child with acceptable semantics, so the jobs half of C4 really is committable independent of the ConPTY spike outcome.
assumptions.basis: D2 phases 'jobs first' on the strength of durable job records + job-object identity, but gate_adapter's stdin sink, job_runner._ACTIVE_LANE/_FOLDER_BUILD serialization, and the SSE tail path are live in-process couplings the intake lists without analyzing; answer_gate in particular requires the supervisor to hold and expose an interactive stdin channel, which is PTY-shaped work smuggled into the 'easy' half.

assumptions.assumption: The restarted dashboard can reconstruct its entire in-memory job bookkeeping (_LIVE, _JOB_DIRS, active-lane locks, attached SSE consumers) from durable records plus supervisor IPC queries — i.e., the dashboard can be made effectively stateless with respect to running work — since 'restart leaves the job running AND the dashboard reporting it live' requires resume-of-life, and the intake itself concedes today's boot reconcile 'reconciles death; it never resumes life.'
assumptions.basis: C4's live-proof criterion; Stage-0 Pillar-4 findings establish the machinery for detecting dead children but contain zero evidence about re-adopting live ones, which is the actually novel engineering in the pillar.

assumptions.assumption: The supervisor NSSM service can run under the same identity and environment as `anchor` (account .\john, claude.exe creds path, PATH, ANCHOR_* env, NO_WINDOW discipline) and its children can be detached from the dashboard's process lifetime (job-object/console inheritance rewired) — otherwise supervisor-spawned Foreman runs fail on credentials or still die with a dashboard restart, silently voiding C4.
assumptions.basis: anchor-runtime-facts memory: the anchor service runs as .\john specifically because claude credentials are per-user; job_runner today attaches children to job objects whose kill-on-close semantics were designed for the opposite goal (die-with-parent); neither the North Star nor intake addresses service identity or job-object rewiring.

assumptions.assumption: The ConPTY-across-processes spike yields a decisive, early yes/no and its failure mode is contained — the plan's phasing assumes PTY scope is the ONLY thing the spike gates, when an economic 'no' also leaves terminal sessions permanently dashboard-owned, meaning `nssm restart anchor` keeps killing live trio terminals forever and the Butler's 'always-on' premise quietly narrows to batch jobs only.
assumptions.basis: GAP-1 and D2 mandate the spike and pre-authorize the honest narrowing, but no acceptance thresholds (latency budget, re-attach semantics, effort cap) are defined, and the downstream Butler cost of the narrowed outcome is not priced anywhere in the North Star.

assumptions.assumption: Everything under .anchor/ is pure runtime state that survives relocation via ANCHOR_DATA_DIR — yet existing durable records store ABSOLUTE paths (registry folder_path, worktree_path, job dirs, discovery.json) minted under the repo-rooted layout, many of those files are currently TRACKED and MODIFIED in git (so 'git status clean' requires untracking committed state, not just .gitignore), and the per-project journal D1 roots at .anchor/projects/<pid>/ moves with it; migrate_data's idempotent copy has never been exercised against a LIVE service mid-write.
assumptions.basis: gitStatus in this session shows .anchor/projects/** as tracked modified files; paths.py resolves lazily but the intake confirms records persist absolute paths; C6 demands the live deployment flip plus a clean healthcheck cycle, an operation with no rehearsal evidence in the repo.

assumptions.assumption: The strangler migration has no hidden flag-days: the ~125 route moves, the frontend extraction, and the auth flip can each be decomposed into steps that are individually green, deployable, and revertible — in particular that switching a route from open to token-gated never strands a cached frontend still calling it the old way (stale-browser class the repo already documents as a known pitfall).
assumptions.basis: C7 and the planning directives bind every increment to a live dashboard; D3 prescribes table-with-fallthrough which covers dispatch but not the auth-semantics flip or the served-JS/route coupling — a token-gated endpoint plus a user's day-old cached JS bundle is a breakage the no-cache headers only partially prevent.

assumptions.assumption: The event schema (envelope {seq, ts, schema_ver, type, actor, payload} + the GAP-3 taxonomy) can be designed well enough NOW, before any real consumer exists beyond the parity gate, that the future Butler can consume it without a breaking rewrite — the journal is explicitly a long-lived contract, yet its only in-effort consumers are derivations of TODAY's views, which under-constrains exactly the fields an agent would need (causality/correlation ids, actor provenance, cross-project ordering).
assumptions.basis: North Star D1 + Oranges framing #1 declare the journal 'the ONE artifact the Butler will consume directly' while the non-goals forbid building any Butler consumer; designing a contract against a consumer you are forbidden to prototype is a classic silent-drift risk two steps downstream.

assumptions.assumption: No concurrent effort mutates the same surfaces mid-flight: the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build, any v12 merge/deploy, and routine live use won't land changes to anchor_gui.py / healthcheck / route surface between this effort's increments — the line-number ground truth in the North Star (5623–10285, 14220–16019, etc.) stays valid long enough for Stage 2 to execute against it.
assumptions.basis: Memory records the ship-v1 Foreman 'parked awaiting John + concurrent build' and v12 'NOT merged — awaiting sign-off'; the North Star sequences only after fix/review-wave-a-2026-07 and is silent on these two live branches, whose merge would shift every hardcoded anchor line and re-fork the frontend blobs mid-extraction.

assumptions.assumption: The daily healthcheck (4,970 lines, five stubbed surface walks) can absorb all four pillars' new gates — parity derivation, supervisor inline seam, cookie-authed endpoint walk, relocated data dir — without itself becoming the flaky bottleneck; its stub seams (ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD, ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND, temp data dirs) are assumed to extend cleanly to a supervisor seam and a journal-bearing data layout.
assumptions.basis: GAP-4 names the seam need for the supervisor only, but C2 (auth walk), C3 (parity in healthcheck), and C6 (clean cycle post-move) each add healthcheck obligations; the healthcheck is John's production alarm — degrading its signal-to-noise costs more than any single pillar delivers.

assumptions.assumption: The two pre-dispatch streaming specials (term_ws upgrade, term_stream2 SSE) and any long-lived-connection routes can be expressed in — or honestly special-cased around — the single declarative route table without violating C2's 'ALL routes dispatch through a single table', since an http.server handler that hijacks the socket for WS does not fit the request-response dispatch shape the table implies.
assumptions.basis: Stage-0 T2 notes term_ws/term_stream2 sit before dispatch at 14223/14230; C2's absolutist phrasing ('all ~125 arms') collides with that mechanical reality unless the table's contract explicitly models upgrade/streaming policies.

assumptions.assumption: anchor_server.py is truly referenced by nothing outside runtime code — no scheduled task, shortcut, John muscle-memory URL on :5000, or external doc depends on it — so deletion is pure win with no ops follow-up.
assumptions.basis: Stage-0 confirms absence from imports, dist manifest, NSSM, launchers, and healthcheck; residual risk is only out-of-repo references (Task Scheduler, browser bookmarks), which one elevated audit closes.

assumptions.assumption: The live restart-survival demonstration (C4) can be staged on the real :8777 service with a real in-flight job without risking John's actual project data or a wedged service — i.e., there exists a safe 'sacrificial but real' job whose survival proves the property, and an elevated shell is available at demo time.
assumptions.basis: C4 explicitly demands proof 'on the real service', a category of test the repo's entire stub discipline (fake_claude, stub PTY, temp data dirs) was built to avoid; nothing yet defines the blast-radius containment for doing it live.

premortem.mode: Frontend extraction stalls at ~60% because the f-string turns out to be structurally server-composed: dozens of _render_* helpers emit conditional HTML blocks (per-lane columns, session tiles, badge variants) that cannot move verbatim into a static file, and re-expressing them client-side is a rewrite the 'no UI redesign' non-goal forbids. The ≥7,000-line shrink is missed and the wave is abandoned half-extracted, leaving TWO frontend sources to keep in sync.
premortem.cause: Nobody measured the interpolation census before locking the success bar; 'data-shaped vs structural' was asserted from a skim of ~2,700 lines, and the ~2,800 lines of _render_* helpers were mentally filed as 'server-side' rather than 'markup the static file will need'.
premortem.mitigation: Stage-2 pre-work: a mechanical census script that classifies every {…} interpolation in generate_html and _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS as data/flag/markup-emitting, with counts, BEFORE wave sizing. If markup-emitting interpolations exceed a small threshold, amend the North Star bar to 'template + bootstrap JSON + a small server-side include layer' up front, not mid-wave. Define the shrink target as a derived number from the census, and gate the wave on the census, not on hope.

premortem.mode: Extraction merges green, Playwright home+project-window checks pass, and two weeks later John's daily use hits silent breakage: the pending-paste flush never fires after a grass advance, WS terminal resize is dead, drag-to-group drops the project, and the v12 dock ignores clicks — all in flows the two-page smoke never exercised. Trust in 'behavior parity' collapses and every subsequent wave gets manually re-verified by John, destroying velocity.
premortem.cause: Parity was defined as 'the two pages load and look right', but ~4,660 lines of client JS is mostly event-handler behavior (WS/SSE, timers, paste flush, resize observers) that a load-time screenshot cannot observe; the escape/f-string-doubling transform ({{→{) is exactly the kind of mechanical change that corrupts one handler in a thousand.
premortem.mitigation: Make the extraction byte-verifiable, not behavior-verifiable: the build step must prove the served JS/CSS is byte-identical (post-de-escaping) to what the f-string emitted before the move, via a golden-file diff gate that renders both paths and compares. Reserve Playwright for the bootstrap-JSON seam only (the one thing that genuinely changed). Add scripted Playwright flows for the top-5 stateful behaviors (terminal open+type, paste flush, drag-to-group, maximize/restore, dock) as a one-time investment before wave 1.

premortem.mode: The entire auth pillar ships, gates pass, and the live box is exactly as open as before: ANCHOR_TOKEN was never set on the NSSM service, so default-deny evaluates to allow-all on the only deployment that matters. Months later the iPhone/Tailscale exposure (already researched and desired) goes live against an unauthenticated data plane and the 'C2 done' checkbox provides false assurance.
premortem.cause: C2 was written conditionally ('when ANCHOR_TOKEN is set') to avoid breaking John's browser mid-migration, and no wave owned the operational act of minting the token, setting it in NSSM AppEnvironment, and doing the one-time cookie handshake on John's devices.
premortem.mitigation: Add an explicit ops-cutover step to the plan with its own gate: mint token → set service env → restart → healthcheck asserts the GET data plane returns 401 tokenless ON THE LIVE :8777. The pillar is not DONE until the live service rejects an unauthenticated /api/rnd/projects. If John declines to run tokened, record that as a North-Star amendment (honest narrowing), never silently.

premortem.mode: The cookie flip lands and three consumer classes break at once: the daily 5AM healthcheck starts failing its endpoint walk (red banner every morning), John's CLI mirror and a couple of personal scripts get 401s, and the hand-rolled WS upgrade rejects the browser because the Cookie header parse or the SameSite attribute doesn't survive the ws:// scheme on some client. The 'fix' becomes a same-day flag-day scramble — precisely the C7 violation the strangler shape was meant to prevent.
premortem.cause: The consumer inventory was scoped to 'the browser'; localhost script/healthcheck/CLI consumers of the open GET plane were never enumerated, and the RFC-6455 path is hand-rolled, so no framework guarantees cookies flow through the 101 upgrade.
premortem.mitigation: Before any route flips: enumerate every consumer of every currently-open route (grep the repo, healthcheck, .bat/.vbs launchers, scheduled tasks) and give each a token path FIRST (Authorization header accepted everywhere, ?token= kept for WS/SSE). Flip routes to enforcing in small reviewed batches with a per-route ANCHOR_AUTH_WARN log-only mode for a soak day — observe who would 401 before anyone does. Spike the cookie-through-WS-upgrade on the real dashboard (desktop + iPhone PWA) before committing D3's 'cookie-based' wording.

premortem.mode: The parity gate never reaches zero and stays permanently red: instrumenting the four named modules missed a half-dozen write sites — handlers in anchor_gui.py that touch index.json directly, rnd_registry lifecycle mutations, boneyard.record_entry callers, healthcheck's own synthetic walks, and the CLI's delegated writes — so journal-derived views chronically miss events. The gate gets marked 'known-flaky', which is indistinguishable from the journal being untrustworthy, killing the pillar's entire value proposition.
premortem.cause: The 'closed set of write sites' was assumed from module names rather than proven; a 18k-line monolith grown over 12 versions has convenience writes scattered in handlers, and the healthcheck/CLI write through partially different paths.
premortem.mitigation: Invert the discovery: build a test-mode tripwire that wraps every open(…,'w')/json.dump under .anchor/ and fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event (allowlist the journal itself). Run the full suite + healthcheck under the tripwire to enumerate the true write-site set mechanically before designing instrumentation. Route all appends through one emit() choke point in a new journal module; forbid direct store writes outside blessed wrappers via a distro.py-style scan.

premortem.mode: 'Zero divergence' proves untestable in the wild: a crash between legacy write and journal append (or vice versa) manufactures one-event divergence; the daily healthcheck derives views while the live service concurrently writes, producing racy false reds; and in one case the JOURNAL is right and the LEGACY store is torn — the gate faithfully reports divergence and the on-call reflex 'fix the journal' actively destroys the recovery record. The red banner John was retrained to trust becomes noise within two weeks.
premortem.cause: The gate was specified as an equality invariant over a non-atomic dual-write observed concurrently, with no ordering discipline, no reconciliation protocol, and no statement of which side wins each divergence class.
premortem.mitigation: Fix the write order by decree (journal-first, then legacy; an orphaned journal event is a benign 'intent' record) and make the gate a QUIESCENT check: healthcheck derives from a snapshot copy (WRITE_LOCK-bracketed or shadow-copied), tolerates a bounded tail window of N-seconds-recent events, and classifies divergences (journal-ahead=OK, legacy-ahead=BUG, conflict=BUG) instead of binary zero/nonzero. Ship a reconcile report tool alongside, and document 'journal-ahead' as the expected crash residue with an idempotent replay.

premortem.mode: The jobs-half of the supervisor split ships but semantics degrade unacceptably: gate answers (AskUserQuestion stdin writes) intermittently miss because the stdin handle now lives across an IPC hop with a reconnect race; tail cursors reset on supervisor restart; cancel tree-kills orphan grandchildren the supervisor can't see; token/cost accounting double-counts. Each is 'small', but together the dashboard's job UX is worse than before the split, and John asks for it to be reverted — un-committing C4's non-negotiable half.
premortem.cause: 'Proxy it over loopback IPC' treated job interaction as a data plane when parts of it (held stdin, process-tree ownership, cursor state) are ownership semantics that don't survive a process boundary without an explicit protocol per interaction.
premortem.mitigation: Before the split, write the IPC contract as a table: every dashboard↔job interaction (launch, tail-since, cancel, gate-answer, cost, swarm-register) with its state owner, failure mode on either side restarting, and idempotency key. Gate the wave on a stub-seam test matrix that kills each side mid-interaction. Keep the gate-answer path synchronous-with-ack (answer is durably queued in the supervisor before the POST returns) so a dropped hop is retryable, never lost.

premortem.mode: The live demo half-succeeds and C4 is quietly missed: after `nssm restart anchor`, the job is still running under the supervisor (survival ✓) but the restarted dashboard shows the lane empty or 'failed' — _LIVE/_JOB_DIRS/lane-locks were rebuilt as 'dead' because boot reconcile still reconciles death rather than resuming life, and re-attaching SSE consumers to a supervisor-held stream was never actually implemented. Success criterion 4's second clause ('reporting it live') fails on the box, after all the waves merged.
premortem.cause: Resume-of-life is a different feature from survive-restart, and the plan let the supervisor wave claim C4 while the dashboard-side resume (registry hydration from supervisor IPC + tail re-subscription + lane-lock reconstruction) was deferred as 'reporting polish'.
premortem.mitigation: Make 'restart mid-job → dashboard shows the SAME job live with a working tail and a working cancel' the wave's literal automated gate (stub seam) AND the live sign-off script, not a narrative claim. Enumerate the in-memory structures (_LIVE, _JOB_DIRS, locks, SSE attach points) in the implementation plan with a rebuild-source column (durable record vs supervisor query); any entry with no rebuild source is a design hole to resolve before EXECUTE.

premortem.mode: Supervisor-spawned Foreman/claude runs fail only in production: the new NSSM service was installed as LocalSystem (the installer default), so claude.exe finds no credentials, or the child inherits the supervisor's job object/console and a supervisor restart now kills all jobs — recreating the exact fate-sharing the split existed to remove, one process to the left. Because tests use the inline seam, everything is green; the failure appears the first time a real lane job runs under the real service.
premortem.cause: Identity/environment (account .\john, creds path, ANCHOR_* env, PATH) and Windows process-lifetime plumbing (job objects, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, detached process groups) are host-configuration facts the inline test seam cannot exercise by construction.
premortem.mitigation: Script the service install (nssm install + ObjectName .\john + AppEnvironmentExtra copied from the anchor service) rather than documenting it; add a healthcheck probe that asks the LIVE supervisor to spawn a trivial claude.exe --version child and report its output; add a second live probe that restarts the SUPERVISOR with a sacrificial child running and asserts the child survived (breakaway verified). Treat these as the wave's sign-off, with the inline seam covering logic only.

premortem.mode: The ConPTY spike returns 'economically infeasible' as the plan allowed — and the honest narrowing turns out to gut the Butler premise: every trio terminal session still dies on `nssm restart anchor`, which happens at every deploy of this very effort's remaining waves, so the re-architecture repeatedly kills John's in-flight planning/build terminals while it lands. The recorded narrowing was treated as a footnote instead of a product decision, and nobody designed the fallback.
premortem.cause: The spike was framed as gating PTY scope only; no one costed the 'no' branch (always-on narrows to batch jobs) or scheduled a mitigation for it, and the effort's own deploy cadence multiplies the pain.
premortem.mitigation: Pre-commit a designed fallback for the 'no' branch before the spike runs: graceful pre-restart drain (close_session park + capture_session_docs + W3 warm-resume seed for every live PTY, automated in the deploy script), so a restart costs a warm reconnect instead of dead context. If the spike says no, the drain ships in the same wave. Also time-box the spike early (Wave 1-adjacent) so the answer shapes sequencing rather than arriving after the supervisor waves.

premortem.mode: The ANCHOR_DATA_DIR relocation bricks the live service on the first restart after cutover: registry folder_path/worktree_path/discovery.json/job-dir records all hold absolute paths minted under C:\dev\Anchor\.anchor, so the relocated service resolves sessions/worktrees that 'don't exist'; the boot orphan-reaper then helpfully deletes worktrees it can't match, destroying parked session state. Meanwhile `git status` still isn't clean because the old .anchor files are TRACKED — gitignore did nothing — and untracking them mid-history collides with the journal now living in the moved tree.
premortem.cause: 'Runtime state' was treated as location-independent when the stores are absolute-path-laden; migrate_data was written for a cold copy and never exercised against live-minted absolute references; git cleanliness needs `git rm --cached` surgery, not ignore rules.
premortem.mitigation: Add a path-audit tool to the wave: scan every durable store for absolute paths under the repo root and emit a rewrite map; migration = stop service → migrate_data → path-rewrite pass → start → healthcheck, as one scripted, rollback-able unit with the old dir preserved read-only for a week. Disarm the boot reaper (dry-run mode) for the first post-move boot. Handle git in a separate commit: git rm --cached the ~62 artifacts + .gitignore, verified by a healthcheck-cycle-then-git-status gate.

premortem.mode: A mid-migration deploy strands John's own browser: a route flipped from open to cookie-gated while his long-lived dashboard tab (open for days, service-worker/PWA-cached JS on the iPad) still calls it the old way; the tab half-works — board renders, terminals 401 — which reads as 'the re-architecture broke terminals' and burns a debugging evening on the documented stale-browser pitfall, now with an auth flavor that no-cache headers don't fix because the cookie handshake needs a real navigation.
premortem.cause: Each route flip is individually green in tests, but the strangler analysis ignored client-side deployment lag: the browser is a distributed-system node that updates on ITS schedule, and the PWA/iPad path caches harder than desktop.
premortem.mitigation: Version the frontend↔backend contract: bootstrap JSON carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, and the server answers a mismatched id with a structured 409 that the (old) client already knows how to turn into a 'reload required' banner — ship that tiny shim in the LAST pre-migration release, before any flips. Sequence auth flips behind a warn-only soak (FM-04) and never flip a route in the same deploy that changes the JS calling it.

premortem.mode: Eighteen months later the Butler effort begins and the journal is unusable as its memory: events lack correlation/causality ids (which session advance caused which job launch), actor provenance (user click vs auto-advance vs healthcheck synthetic), and cross-project ordering, because the only consumer that shaped the schema was a parity gate that re-derives today's views. schema_ver=2 becomes a breaking rewrite plus a backfill migration over a year of production events — the exact contract-rot the journal existed to prevent.
premortem.cause: Schema design was validated against derivability of current views (a low bar the legacy stores already meet) instead of against the Butler's known query shapes; healthcheck synthetics also pollute the stream with no way to filter them.
premortem.mitigation: Write three concrete Butler user stories NOW ('what happened on project X this week', 'what did the user decide vs what auto-advanced', 'which job did this doc come from') and require the Stage-2 schema to answer them from envelope fields alone: mandatory correlation_id, causation_id, actor{kind,id}, monotonic per-project seq + wall ts, and a synthetic/healthcheck actor kind. Reserve-and-ignore beats retrofit. Add a schema-evolution rule (additive-only within a major ver) to the journal module docstring as a binding convention.

premortem.mode: Stage 2's line-number ground truth is fiction by EXECUTE time: the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build lands its onboarding changes, a v12 hotfix touches anchor_gui.py, and routine live use shifts the file by a few hundred lines — the extraction wave's 'move lines 5623–10285' instructions mis-slice the blob, and the Foreman agent, trusting the plan, ships a frontend missing the dock JS. Detection is late because the two-page Playwright check (FM-02) passes.
premortem.cause: The North Star froze line numbers as facts in a repo with at least one parked concurrent build and daily live use; nothing in the plan re-derives them at execution time.
premortem.mitigation: Never encode line numbers in the implementation plan — encode ANCHORS (the _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS assignment, the generate_html def, sentinel comments) plus a pre-wave freshness gate that re-locates each anchor and fails loudly on ambiguity. Declare a soft merge-freeze on anchor_gui.py for concurrent efforts during the extraction wave specifically (the one wave that can't tolerate drift), coordinated with the parked v1 build's schedule.

premortem.mode: The healthcheck becomes the effort's bottleneck and boy-who-cried-wolf: after absorbing the parity derivation, supervisor seam, cookie walk, and relocated-data-dir walk, the 5AM run's wall time triples and its false-red rate (concurrency in the parity gate, port races in the supervisor probe) means the banner is red twice a week for non-bugs. John stops reading it — exactly the observability regression a re-architecture for observability cannot afford.
premortem.cause: Four pillars each independently added 'and the healthcheck gates it' without a budget for the check's runtime, flake rate, or the fact that its stub seams were designed for in-process fakes, not a second service.
premortem.mitigation: Give the healthcheck an explicit SLO in the plan (wall-time cap, zero-known-flakes policy) and add new walks behind the same discipline as product code: each new check ships with its own quiescence strategy (FM-06), retries-with-classification, and an 'Auto-fixes applied' degradation path rather than a red. Run the four new walks nightly in CI-style repetition (20×) before wiring them into the 5AM run.

premortem.mode: C2's 'ALL routes through a single table' is enforced literally and the WS/SSE specials get mangled: the term_ws socket hijack is forced through the request-response table shape, subtly breaking the 401-before-101 ordering (auth now runs after headers are consumed) or buffering SSE through a generic responder that adds latency/heartbeat regressions to live terminals. Alternatively the specials stay outside the table but undeclared, and the auth audit misses them — the two most sensitive routes are the two the default-deny table doesn't govern.
premortem.cause: The success criterion's absolutist wording collided with http.server reality (socket-hijacking handlers aren't request-response), and neither 'force it in' nor 'silently exempt it' was written down as the decision.
premortem.mitigation: Amend the table contract explicitly in Stage 2: every route — including streaming/upgrade specials — must have a ROW (path, auth policy, handler kind: standard|stream|upgrade), and the default-deny audit runs over rows, but dispatch for kind≠standard may be honestly special-cased at the pre-dispatch hook with the row's auth check invoked FIRST (401-before-101 preserved as an explicit test). The invariant becomes 'no route exists without a declared row', which is auditable, instead of 'one dispatch shape', which is false.

premortem.mode: anchor_server.py is deleted and a week later something breaks off-repo: a forgotten scheduled task or an old shortcut in John's Start Menu tries :5000 nightly and logs errors, or an archived doc's instructions send a collaborator (the ship-v1 audience) to a dead port. Trivial individually — but it lands as 'the re-architecture broke something' during the exact window trust in never-broken increments is being established.
premortem.cause: 'Referenced by nothing' was verified by repo grep only; Windows scheduled tasks, .lnk shortcuts, and human muscle memory live outside the repo.
premortem.mitigation: Before deletion: one scheduled-tasks + Start-Menu/Desktop shortcut sweep (Get-ScheduledTask, search *.lnk targets) and a grep of the _archive/ docs; then delete but keep a one-line tombstone note in the changelog. Cheap, bounded, closes the class.

premortem.mode: The live C4 demo itself causes the incident: the 'sacrificial' job chosen for the restart demo is launched in a real project and its half-configured supervisor handoff wedges the lane lock, or the demo requires an elevated shell John isn't at the keyboard to provide, so the demo gets skipped, the criterion is signed off from the stub-seam test alone, and FM-08/FM-09's production-only failures ship undetected.
premortem.cause: The demo was specified as a property ('demonstrated on the real service') without a runbook: no sacrificial project, no rollback, no scheduling of John's elevated shell, so under deadline pressure it degrades to 'the tests prove it'.
premortem.mitigation: Write the demo as a runbook artifact in the plan: a dedicated throwaway R&D project (real registry, real service, worthless content), a long-running but harmless real job (a fake_claude-driven or sleep-shaped lane job launched through the REAL path, not the stub seam), the exact elevated commands, expected observations, and the rollback (supervisor stop + lane-lock clear). Schedule it WITH John as a wave sign-off event; the criterion is unmet — honestly — until the runbook has been executed once.

premortem.mode: Dual-write throughput/locking degrades the live dashboard: every mutation now takes the journal append (open, lock, write, fsync, close per event under WRITE_LOCK) on top of the legacy write, and hot paths — PTY-driven doc persists, per-tick job bookkeeping, healthcheck's synthetic walks — turn the board sluggish, echoing the pre-2026-06-16 O(everything) dashboard regression John already lived through once.
premortem.cause: The journal was designed for correctness (append-only, fsync'd) with no throughput budget; event emission was wired into per-tick paths rather than mutation-of-record boundaries only.
premortem.mitigation: Scope the taxonomy to mutation-of-record boundaries explicitly (the C3 list) and exclude per-tick/telemetry writes by rule; one appender per project with an O(1) append (open-append-close, fsync batched or configurable); add a perf gate to the wave — journal-on vs journal-off timing of the healthcheck's v2–v5 walks with a hard regression budget (e.g. <5%).

premortem.mode: The four pillars interleave into a combinatorial deploy mess: the supervisor wave needs the route table's IPC endpoints, the auth flip needs the extracted frontend's cookie handshake, the journal parity gate needs the data-dir relocation to have settled — and a mid-sequence failure (any of FM-04/08/11) forces a revert that other merged waves now depend on. 'Never-broken increments' holds per-wave but not for the sequence, and the effort stalls two-thirds done for a month in a hybrid state nobody fully understands.
premortem.cause: Independence between pillars was assumed at North-Star altitude; the dependency edges only appear at implementation grain, and no revert-compatibility rule was set for cross-pillar coupling.
premortem.mitigation: Stage 2 must draw the cross-pillar dependency DAG explicitly and order waves so each merged wave is revertible WITHOUT reverting later-merged waves (revert-compatibility as a stated rule, tested by a 'can we turn this off' flag per pillar: journal emission flag, auth warn/enforce flag, supervisor inline-vs-service flag). Hybrid states become named, supported configurations rather than accidents.

ideas.idea: Interpolation census pre-gate: a mechanical script that classifies EVERY {…} interpolation in generate_html and render_project_window_html (and confirms _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS has zero) as data/flag/markup-emitting, with counts, run BEFORE wave sizing; the ≥7,000-line shrink target becomes a derived number from the census, and the extraction wave is gated on the census output, not on hope.
ideas.note: Directly disposes FM-1; receipt: the f-string spans 10966–13671 with real {expr} interpolations — their true character is currently unmeasured.

ideas.idea: Byte-parity golden-file gate for the extraction: a build/test step renders the page via the OLD f-string path and the NEW static-file+bootstrap path and diffs the emitted JS/CSS byte-for-byte (post-de-escaping of {{/}}); Playwright is reserved for the one thing that genuinely changed — the bootstrap-JSON seam.
ideas.note: FM-2 mitigation: makes parity byte-verifiable, not vibe-verifiable; the two-page smoke can't catch dock/paste/drag regressions but a byte diff can't miss them.

ideas.idea: window.ANCHOR_BOOT bootstrap JSON contract: a single small server-injected JSON object (token presence, project id, build id, feature flags, initial counts) is the ONLY server→client state channel; everything else in the extracted JS reads from it or from existing API calls; the contract is a documented, versioned dict in one module.
ideas.note: North Star names 'a small bootstrap JSON' — this makes it a reviewable contract instead of ad-hoc globals.

ideas.idea: Anchor-based slicing, never line numbers: the implementation plan encodes extraction targets as structural anchors (the _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS assignment, the generate_html def, sentinel comments inserted in a tiny pre-wave commit) plus a freshness gate that re-locates each anchor and fails loudly on ambiguity before EXECUTE.
ideas.note: FM-14: the file WILL drift between Stage 2 and EXECUTE (parked ship-v1 build, hotfixes); line 5623 is fiction by then.

ideas.idea: One-time Playwright investment before wave 1: scripted flows for the top-5 stateful behaviors (terminal open+type via stub PTY, pending-paste flush, drag-to-group, maximize/restore, v12 dock click) that run in the extraction gate AND remain as permanent regression assets for every later pillar.
ideas.note: FM-2; receipt: these five flows are exactly the ones the existing two-page smoke never exercises, and C2's cookie flip + C4's re-attach will need the same harness — triple use.

ideas.idea: Serve the extracted frontend through the EXISTING traversal-safe asset-route idiom (resolve()+relative_to, ValueError→None) already proven 4× in the repo (anchor_term_asset 678, xterm_asset 707, brand_asset 743, katex_asset) — one new static root, zero new security surface.
ideas.note: Reuses a battle-tested pattern; the North Star names this idiom explicitly.

ideas.idea: Content-hash cache-busting on the new static files (?v=<hash8> minted at startup from the file bytes), so a deploy always invalidates John's long-lived tabs and the documented stale-browser pitfall doesn't gain a static-file flavor.
ideas.note: FM-12 adjacent; the server currently sends no-cache headers on the monolithic page — static files change the caching story and must not regress it.

ideas.idea: Frontend↔backend contract versioning shim shipped in the LAST pre-migration release: ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, the server answers a mismatch with a structured 409 the old client renders as a 'reload required' banner — so no later wave can strand a stale tab or PWA-cached iPad client.
ideas.note: FM-12: the shim must predate every flip; it is tiny and pays for itself the first time a route changes under an open tab.

ideas.idea: Soft merge-freeze on anchor_gui.py declared for the extraction wave specifically, coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build's schedule — the one wave that cannot tolerate concurrent drift gets the one narrow freeze, keeping the no-multi-day-freeze rule intact for everything else.
ideas.note: FM-14 second half; a file-scoped soak of days, not a project freeze — compatible with the C7 constraint.

ideas.idea: Route table where EVERY route — including streaming/upgrade specials — has a ROW (method, pattern, auth policy, handler kind: standard|stream|upgrade); the default-deny audit runs over rows; dispatch for kind≠standard is honestly special-cased at the pre-dispatch hook with the row's auth check invoked FIRST. The auditable invariant is 'no route exists without a declared row', not 'one dispatch shape'.
ideas.note: FM-16: term_ws (14223) and term_stream2 (14230) are already pre-dispatch specials; forcing them through a request-response shape would break 401-before-101.

ideas.idea: Explicit 401-before-101 regression test for term_ws: an unauthenticated upgrade attempt must receive 401 before any 101/handshake bytes, asserted at the socket level — preserving the existing hand-rolled RFC-6455 ordering through the table migration.
ideas.note: FM-16; the two most sensitive routes must be the two the audit provably governs.

ideas.idea: ANCHOR_AUTH_WARN log-only mode: each route batch flips to 'warn' first (log who WOULD 401, allow through) for a soak day on the live service, then to 'enforce' — with the warn log reviewed as a gate artifact before enforcement.
ideas.note: FM-4: observes the healthcheck's 5AM walk, CLI mirror, launchers, and any forgotten script before anyone gets a 401.

ideas.idea: Consumer enumeration pre-work: grep-driven inventory of every caller of every currently-open route (repo code, anchor_healthcheck.py's endpoint walk, .bat/.vbs launchers, scheduled tasks, personal scripts dir) and give each a token path FIRST — Authorization header accepted everywhere, ?token= retained only for WS/SSE.
ideas.note: FM-4; bounded work — the open GET plane is 9 named routes and the consumer set is mostly in-repo.

ideas.idea: Cookie-through-WS-upgrade spike on the REAL clients (desktop browser + iPhone PWA over Tailscale HTTPS) before committing D3's cookie wording — verifying the Cookie header survives the ws:// upgrade and SameSite settings on both, with ?token= as the declared WS fallback if it doesn't.
ideas.note: FM-4 tail risk; the anchor-as-app research already targets iPhone/Tailscale, so the PWA client is a known future consumer, not hypothetical.

ideas.idea: Ops-cutover gate with teeth: the C2 wave is not DONE until a healthcheck probe asserts the LIVE :8777 returns 401 on tokenless /api/rnd/projects — i.e. mint token → set NSSM AppEnvironmentExtra → restart → live assert. If John declines to run tokened, that is recorded as a North-Star amendment, never silently.
ideas.note: FM-3: default-deny that evaluates to allow-all on the only deployment that matters is a checkbox, not security.

ideas.idea: Strangler dispatch with fallthrough: the table dispatches first; unmatched requests fall through to the legacy if-elif chains; branches migrate in small reviewed batches; a coverage test counts remaining legacy arms so progress is measurable and the audit knows what the table does NOT yet govern.
ideas.note: D3 mandates strangler-style; the arm-count test turns 'migration in progress' into a number.

ideas.idea: Handlers become module-level functions as they migrate into the table — which kills the os/datetime in-branch import shadowing class (14506, 16063, 15019, 16911) as a free structural consequence; add a distro.py-style AST scan that fails on any in-method import shadowing a module-level name so the class can't return.
ideas.note: C2 names 'zero in-branch imports shadowing module names'; the scan makes it enforced-by-construction, matching the pillar's own philosophy.

ideas.idea: The reviewed open-allowlist as a checked-in artifact: a short OPEN_ROUTES table in the route module with a mandatory justification string per entry, plus a test asserting the set matches exactly — any new open route requires editing the reviewed file, making review structural.
ideas.note: Turns 'explicit, reviewed allowlist' from process into code.

ideas.idea: journal.py with ONE emit() choke point: all appends go through a single function (schema validation, seq assignment, atomic append under WRITE_LOCK); a distro.py-style scan forbids json.dump/open-for-write to journal paths outside the module, and blessed legacy-store wrappers are the only places emit() is called from.
ideas.note: FM-5 structural fix: instrumentation-by-choke-point instead of instrumentation-by-hunting.

ideas.idea: Write-site tripwire to discover the TRUE mutation set mechanically: a test-mode wrapper around file writes under .anchor/ that fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event (journal itself allowlisted); run the full suite + healthcheck under it to enumerate write sites BEFORE designing instrumentation, and keep it running forever as the completeness gate.
ideas.note: FM-5: inverts discovery — the 'half-dozen missed write sites' (direct index.json touches in anchor_gui, rnd_registry lifecycle, boneyard callers) get found by machine, not memory.

ideas.idea: Journal-first write order by decree: emit the event, THEN write the legacy store — an orphaned journal event is a benign 'intent' record, while the reverse orphan is a lost event; document 'journal-ahead' as expected crash residue with an idempotent replay path.
ideas.note: FM-6 first half: fixes the crash-window semantics so divergence has a defined meaning.

ideas.idea: Quiescent, classifying parity gate: the healthcheck derives views from a WRITE_LOCK-bracketed snapshot copy, tolerates a bounded tail window of recent events, and classifies divergence (journal-ahead=OK/crash-residue, legacy-ahead=BUG, conflict=BUG) instead of binary zero/nonzero — with a reconcile-report tool shipped alongside.
ideas.note: FM-6 second half: 'zero divergence' stays meaningful under live concurrent writes instead of becoming known-flaky noise.

ideas.idea: Butler-shaped event envelope, reserve-and-ignore: mandatory correlation_id, causation_id, actor{kind,id} (user-click | auto-advance | healthcheck-synthetic | cli), monotonic per-project seq + wall ts, schema_ver — validated against three concrete written Butler user stories ('what happened on project X this week', 'what did the user decide vs auto-advance', 'which job produced this doc') answerable from envelope fields alone.
ideas.note: FM-13: the parity gate alone would shape a schema that rots; the Butler is the journal's real customer and its stories cost one page now vs a backfill migration later.

ideas.idea: Schema-evolution rule as a binding convention in the journal module docstring: additive-only within a major schema_ver, unknown-field-tolerant readers, and a test that round-trips a v1 event through the v-current reader.
ideas.note: FM-13 tail: makes schema_ver=2 an addition, not a rewrite.

ideas.idea: Recovery tool as a first-class deliverable: rebuild_index.py re-derives a deleted/torn index.json (and sessions.json rows) from the journal, proven in a test that deletes the index mid-suite and in a documented operator runbook — the 'lost from an index' class becomes recoverable-by-construction with a demonstrated recovery.
ideas.note: C3 mandates it; making it a runbook (not just a test) means the first real torn-index incident has a rehearsed answer.

ideas.idea: Journal perf budget gate: time the healthcheck's v2–v5 walks journal-on vs journal-off with a hard regression budget (<5%); one appender per project, O(1) open-append-close, fsync policy configurable; per-tick/telemetry writes excluded from the taxonomy BY RULE (mutation-of-record boundaries only, per the C3 list).
ideas.note: FM-19: John already lived through one O(everything) dashboard regression; the budget makes 'dual-write is cheap' a measured claim.

ideas.idea: IPC contract table as a Stage-2 artifact: every dashboard↔job interaction (launch, tail-since, cancel, gate-answer, cost/rollup, swarm-register) gets a row with state owner, idempotency key, and defined behavior when EITHER side restarts mid-interaction — and the supervisor wave's stub-seam test matrix kills each side mid-interaction per row.
ideas.note: FM-7: the degrade-by-a-thousand-cuts failure is prevented by enumerating the cuts up front.

ideas.idea: Gate-answer durability: an AskUserQuestion answer is durably queued in the supervisor (persisted to the job dir) and ACKed before the dashboard POST returns — a dropped IPC hop is retryable, never lost; the stdin write happens supervisor-side against the handle it owns.
ideas.note: FM-7's worst cut isolated: gate answers are the one interaction where a silent miss wedges a live Foreman run.

ideas.idea: 'Restart mid-job → same job live, tail works, cancel works' as the LITERAL automated gate: a stub-seam test that restarts the dashboard side with a job in flight and asserts the restarted dashboard lists the SAME job_id as running, serves an advancing tail cursor, and can cancel it — plus the same script executed live as the sign-off.
ideas.note: FM-8: C4's second clause ('reporting it live') is the half that quietly fails; make it the gate's literal assertion.

ideas.idea: In-memory-structure rebuild table in the implementation plan: every dashboard-side structure (_LIVE, _JOB_DIRS, _ACTIVE_LANE, _FOLDER_BUILD, lane locks, SSE attach points) gets a rebuild-source column (durable record | supervisor query); any row with no rebuild source is a named design hole that must be resolved before EXECUTE.
ideas.note: FM-8: boot reconcile today 'reconciles death, never resumes life' — this table is the resume-life design forced into writing.

ideas.idea: Scripted supervisor service install: install_supervisor.ps1 does nssm install + ObjectName .\john + AppEnvironmentExtra cloned from the anchor service + CREATE_NO_WINDOW discipline — scripted, not documented — because the anchor service itself runs as .\john and claude.exe credentials live in John's profile.
ideas.note: FM-9: LocalSystem-default is the classic production-only failure; the memory file confirms the account fact (re-verified 2026-06-15).

ideas.idea: Two live healthcheck probes for the supervisor: (a) ask the LIVE supervisor to spawn a trivial claude.exe --version child and report output (credentials + PATH proven under the real service account); (b) restart the SUPERVISOR with a sacrificial child running and assert the child survived (job-object breakaway proven) — the inline seam covers logic only, never these.
ideas.note: FM-9: both failure modes are invisible to inline-seam tests by construction; only live probes can see them.

ideas.idea: ConPTY-across-processes spike scheduled Wave-1-adjacent and time-boxed, with the acceptance question written before it runs (latency bound, re-attach behavior, complexity budget) — so its answer shapes the supervisor sequencing instead of arriving after the supervisor waves have shipped.
ideas.note: Planning directive says EARLY explicitly; GAP-1 is the effort's one genuine unknown.

ideas.idea: Pre-designed fallback for the spike's 'no' branch, shipped in the SAME wave as the narrowing: a graceful pre-restart drain in the deploy script — close_session park + capture_session_docs + W3 warm-resume seed for every live PTY — so `nssm restart anchor` costs a warm reconnect, not dead context, for every remaining deploy of this very effort.
ideas.note: FM-10: the narrowing is a product decision, not a footnote; the drain reuses shipped machinery (crucible-improve W3/W6), so it's cheap.

ideas.idea: ANCHOR_SUPERVISOR=inline|external seam from day one: the supervisor's API is a Python interface with two implementations — in-process (tests, healthcheck, degraded mode) and loopback-HTTP client (production) — so the 4,970-line healthcheck and the test suite never need a second real process, and 'supervisor down' has a defined degraded behavior.
ideas.note: GAP-4 disposal; also gives FM-20 its supervisor off-switch for free.

ideas.idea: C4 live demo as a runbook artifact executed WITH John: a dedicated throwaway R&D project on the real service, a harmless long-running real job through the REAL launch path (fake_claude-driven), the exact elevated commands, expected observations, and rollback steps (supervisor stop + lane-lock clear); the criterion is honestly unmet until the runbook has run once.
ideas.note: FM-18: keeps the demo from either causing an incident or being silently skipped.

ideas.idea: anchor_md.py shared parsing module: extract the byte-identical twin parsers (anchor_gui 194–331 / anchor.py 127–178 plus the companion project/inbox/archived parsers) into one module imported by both, with a golden-corpus test (today's real markdown files parsed identically pre/post) as the de-fork gate.
ideas.note: C5 verbatim; byte-identical twins make this near-zero-risk, and the golden corpus proves it.

ideas.idea: Pre-deletion sweep for anchor_server.py: Get-ScheduledTask scan, Start-Menu/Desktop *.lnk target search for :5000/anchor_server, grep of _archive/ docs for instructions pointing at it — then delete with a one-line tombstone in the changelog.
ideas.note: FM-17: cheap, bounded, closes the off-repo-consumer class during the trust-building window.

ideas.idea: Path-audit tool for the data-dir move: scan every durable store (registry folder_path, worktree_path, discovery.json, job dirs, session records) for absolute paths under the repo root and emit a rewrite map; migration = stop service → migrate_data → path-rewrite → start → healthcheck as ONE scripted, rollback-able unit with the old dir preserved read-only for a week.
ideas.note: FM-11: paths.py's seam moves the ROOT but nothing rewrites the absolute paths already minted under it.

ideas.idea: Boot-reaper dry-run mode for the first post-move boot: worktrees.reap_orphans runs in report-only mode (ANCHOR_REAPER_DRYRUN) for the first boot after relocation, so path-resolution misses can't cascade into deleted parked-session worktrees; armed again only after a clean report.
ideas.note: FM-11's destructive tail: the reaper 'helpfully' deleting worktrees it can't match is the unrecoverable part.

ideas.idea: Git hygiene as its own commit + gate: git rm --cached the ~62 tracked runtime artifacts + .gitignore them (separate from the physical move), then a gate that runs a full healthcheck cycle and asserts `git status --porcelain` is empty — C6's 'stays clean' clause verified, not assumed.
ideas.note: FM-11: gitignore alone does nothing for TRACKED files; the two-step (untrack, then verify-through-a-cycle) is the honest closure.

ideas.idea: Cross-pillar dependency DAG with revert-compatibility as a stated Stage-2 rule: waves ordered so each merged wave is revertible WITHOUT reverting later-merged waves, tested by per-pillar off-switches — journal emission flag, auth warn/enforce flag, supervisor inline/external flag, static-vs-embedded frontend flag — making hybrid states named, supported configurations.
ideas.note: FM-20: 'never-broken increments' must hold for the SEQUENCE, not just per-wave; the flags make it testable.

ideas.idea: Healthcheck SLO in the plan: a wall-time cap and zero-known-flakes policy for the 5AM run; each new walk (parity gate, supervisor probes, cookie walk, relocated-data-dir walk) ships with its own quiescence strategy, retry-with-classification, and an 'Auto-fixes applied' degradation path — and runs 20× in nightly repetition before being wired into the 5AM run.
ideas.note: FM-15: a re-architecture FOR observability cannot afford to train John to ignore the red banner.

ideas.idea: Per-wave live-service smoke in the merge ritual: every wave's merge checklist ends with 'nssm restart anchor (or the drain script) → GET / 200 → one project window loads → healthcheck on-demand green' — a 5-minute scripted verification that C7 held on the box, not just in CI.
ideas.note: C7 is a property of the LIVE service; the suite alone can't see NSSM/env/port realities.

ideas.idea: Auth flips never ship in the same deploy as the JS that calls the flipped routes: a sequencing rule in the plan (frontend change lands, soaks; route enforce follows) so a half-cached client never meets a newly-gated endpoint.
ideas.note: FM-12's sequencing half, complementing the B-08 shim.

ideas.idea: Route-table introspection endpoint (/api/routes, token-authed): dumps the live table — path, method, auth policy, handler kind, legacy-or-migrated — giving the auth audit, the healthcheck, and eventually the Butler a machine-readable API contract.

ideas.idea: Journal tail CLI (`anchor.py rnd events <pid> [--since seq]`): a read-only inspection mirror over the per-project journal, following the established v3–v12 CLI-mirror convention — immediately useful for debugging dual-write, and the first taste of the journal as a queryable record.
ideas.note: Consistent with the repo's read-only CLI-mirror pattern; doubles as the reconcile-report viewer.

ideas.idea: Butler v0 prototype: a read-only daily digest agent that consumes the journal and posts 'what happened this week' summaries.
ideas.note: Explicit non-goal ('NOT building the Butler itself'); park it — the B-23 schema stories keep the door open.

ideas.idea: Promote the journal to source of truth with a read-path cutover and legacy-store retirement.
ideas.note: Explicit non-goal; D1 defers this to a later effort. Parked with the note that B-21/B-22's semantics were designed to make the cutover safe later.

ideas.idea: SQLite-backed event index for fast journal queries (seq/correlation lookups).
ideas.note: Violates 'no new storage engines / no SQLite' verbatim; JSONL + in-memory derivation is sufficient at Anchor's scale.

ideas.idea: Decompose terminal_session.py (3,547 lines) while the supervisor work is touching its seams anyway.
ideas.note: Explicitly excluded (Plan-1 Wave D item 13, A5); tempting adjacency is exactly how scope creep happens — park it.

ideas.idea: Enable the iPhone/Tailscale exposure (Tailscale Serve HTTPS + PWA manifest) once the auth pillar lands, since C2 removes the blocker the anchor-as-app research identified.
ideas.note: C2 is the enabler but exposure itself is a separate effort; B-14's PWA spike keeps this future compatible without absorbing it.

ideas.idea: Modernize the frontend stack (bundler, framework, TypeScript) as part of the extraction since the JS is being moved anyway.
ideas.note: Violates 'NOT a UI redesign' and stdlib-only build discipline; extraction is verbatim by decree — parity is the whole safety argument.

ideas.idea: Cross-project GLOBAL journal aggregator (one merged event stream across all projects with cross-project ordering).
ideas.note: C3 is per-project by design; a Butler-era need at most. B-23's per-project seq + wall ts makes later merging possible without building it now.

ideas.idea: Supervisor also absorbs the preview_server and zombie-hunter lifecycles so ALL child processes have one owner.
ideas.note: Attractive symmetry but C4 scopes 'spawned lane jobs' + PTYs-behind-spike only; absorbing more surface area multiplies FM-7/FM-8 risk in the same wave. Park as a natural follow-on.

ideas.idea: Idempotent event replay tool: re-applying the journal against the legacy stores converges them (bounded, dry-run-first) — the operational answer to a legacy-ahead or conflict divergence classification.
ideas.note: Completes FM-6's mitigation: classification (B-22) without a repair verb leaves the on-call reflex dangerous; replay makes journal-ahead residue self-healing.

ideas.idea: Tail-cursor durability across supervisor restarts: the supervisor persists per-job read offsets/log positions in the job dir so /api/rnd/tail cursors survive a supervisor restart without resetting — covered by a row in the B-27 contract table and a kill-mid-tail test.
ideas.note: FM-7 named tail-cursor reset explicitly; job logs are already durable files, so the fix is offset bookkeeping, not new plumbing.

ideas.idea: Frontend extraction lands as MULTIPLE increments in dependency order — _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS first (raw string, zero interpolations, pure verbatim move), then the project-window HTML/CSS shell, then the generate_html f-string (the only genuinely fiddly one, gated on the B-01 census) — each independently merged, byte-gated, and live-smoked.
ideas.note: Sequencing by risk: the 4,660-line raw string is the cheap 25% of the shrink and proves the pipeline before the hard part; aligns C1 with C7's increment rule.

ideas.idea: Healthcheck consumes the route table for its endpoint walk: instead of a hand-maintained URL list, the 5AM walk iterates the declared rows (skipping kind=upgrade), asserting auth behavior per declared policy — new routes are automatically walked and an undeclared route can't hide from the daily check.
ideas.note: Oranges: couples C2's table to C7's healthcheck so the audit runs every morning, not once at review time.

ideas.idea: Named hybrid-state matrix in the plan: the supported combinations of the four pillar flags (e.g. 'frontend extracted + auth warn-only + journal on + supervisor inline') each get a one-line support statement and a healthcheck assertion of the CURRENT configuration, so mid-sequence reality is always a named state.
ideas.note: FM-20's 'hybrid state nobody fully understands' becomes impossible by naming; cheap because the flags exist per B-42.
